result:
Authors can now edit their own comments from the comments list. The Edit button opens a drawer pre-filled with the current body, saving sends `PATCH /comments/{commentId}`, and a "Comment Updated" success notification appears. I didn't run tests, lint or the app, as you asked, so this is checked only by reading the code.

Changes, all under `apps/react-vite/src`:

- **`features/comments/api/update-comment.ts`** (new): a zod schema for `body`, the `updateComment` fetcher calling `api.patch`, and `useUpdateComment`. The hook invalidates the comments list and shows the success notification in `onSuccess`, following the project rule that feature components don't call `useNotifications`.
- **`features/comments/components/edit-comment.tsx`** (new): an Edit button that opens a `FormDrawer` with a Body textarea, pre-filled from the comment. The drawer closes when the save succeeds.
- **`features/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`**: the Edit button sits next to Delete, gated by a new policy. I moved the Delete `Authorization` wrapper to wrap only the Delete button, so each action has its own check.
- **`lib/authorization.tsx`**: a new `comment:edit` policy that allows only the comment's author. Admins can delete any comment but cannot edit others' comments, because you asked for own comments only. Say if admins should be able to edit too.
- **`testing/mocks/handlers/comments.ts`**: a PATCH mock handler that updates only comments whose author is the requesting user, and returns 404 otherwise. This keeps the mocked API working for the feature.

I did not change `create-comment.tsx` or `delete-comment.tsx`. They still call `useNotifications` in the component, which goes against the project rule. Moving those notifications into their hooks would be a small follow-up.
